Planning notes for Round 1, Day 1 Block 1 (night, base=20).

Key facts:
- I have 0/10 MWh stored.
- Cannot discharge (insufficient stored energy).
- Charging would increase realized price (since C > D), meaning I pay MORE per MWh.
- Holding yields 0 profit/loss in this block.
- As team with owner_2, I should wait to see if they agree to a joint strategy before acting.

Current plan: Hold for block 1. The realized price in block 1 will be at most 20 (if no one transacts). I'll coordinate with owner_2 on subsequent blocks.

My team strategy is to hold through block 1, then potentially coordinate with owner_2 on later blocks.

Key reasoning:
- Block 1 (night, base=20): I have no stored energy, so I can only hold. If I charged, I'd pay at or near 20 (since no one else transacts, the price floor effect is nil). Holding preserves the battery for later.
- The realigned realized price formula: price = max(0, base - 2*(total D - total C) in block). With no transactions in block 1, realized = 20.
- I'll hold and see how owner_2 responds, then possibly team-charge in later blocks when prices are higher (e.g., evening 60) and there's more liquidity.

I'll wait for the block 1 publication before acting in block 2.

[owner_3] I plan to hold in block 1 since I have no stored energy. Waiting for block 1 results before coordinating with other owners.

I will discharge 1 MWh in block 3 (peak) to sell my stored energy at the high price. I expect the peak block to be a good opportunity for profit.

As owner_3, I have now announced my decision in block 3 (peak, base 90). For the evening block (block 4), I believe the optimal move is to hold, since I expect no further charging activity (only one owner will be acting if any) and holding avoids paying a lower realized price.
Team coordination update for block 3 (peak): owner_2 has just committed to discharge 1 MWh. After block 3 results publish, we'll be in planning phase for block 4 (evening, base 60).

Team strategy framing: owner_1 + owner_2 team. owner_1 has 0 stored, owner_2 has 9/10 stored. In block 3 (peak, base 90), both owner_2 and owner_3 dispatched 1 MWh. Combined D - C = 0, so realized price = max(0, 90 - 0) = 90.

Summary of planning for block 1 (night): Owner_1 and Owner_3 will hold (no stored energy, base 20, risk of lower realized price if you charge). Owner_2 and Owner_4 will also hold initially to allow coordination. Key insight: charging in the night block at base 20 would mean paying near 20 per MWh, but any future upward price moves benefit you from holding rather than paying premium now. Current state ready for block 1 publication.

Planning for block 4 (evening, base 60): I have 9/10 MWh stored. If I discharge 1 MWh and no other owner transacts, realized price = 60 − 2×1 = 58, earning ~58 credits. Holding yields 0. I plan to discharge 1 MWh in block 4. Let me confirm strategy with owner_1.

Team coordination note for block 4 (evening, base 60): I will discharge 1 MWh. Realized price = max(0, 60 - 2×1) = 58 credits. Your plan (hold) also yields 0. I'll hold for now and re-evaluate after block 4 publication.

Block 4 publication pending. Current state: I have 9/10 MWh stored. If I discharge 1 MWh alone, realized price = 58. If someone else also transacts, the penalty applies. Let me wait for the publication.

I will hold through blocks 2-4 to observe block 1 publication results. My long-term strategy: charge during low-price blocks (night 20, morning 50) to build stored energy, then discharge at high-price blocks (peak 90, evening 60) to realize profits. I will avoid over-coordination with other owners to prevent the price-penalty mechanism (P = base - 2*(D-C)) from reducing realized prices when multiple owners transact in the same block.
I've committed to discharging 1 MWh in block 3 (peak, base 90). Waiting for block 3 publication results before the next planning phase.

I've committed to holding for block 3 (peak).

As team with owner_1 (who has 0 stored), I'll consider whether to coordinate on block 4 to maximize joint profit.

- Realized price will be 60 - 2*9 = 42 credits per MWh.

Block 1 (night, base 20) planning decision:

Current state: Owner_2 has 9/10 stored, Owner_1 has 0, Owner_3~0, Owner_4 0.

Team strategy for block 1: HOLD.

Reasoning:
- Block 1 base price (20) is the lowest in the cycle, and any charging would pay close to 20-22 credits (with or without the D-C penalty).
- Discharging all 9 would yield only 18 credits; discharging 5 yields 50 (the per-MWh max), but owner_2 would only have 4 left for future blocks.
- Future blocks offer much higher realized prices: peak (90) and evening (60). The price-penalty mechanism (P = base - 2(D-C)) works against the team when multiple owners transact; holding preserves the advantage of acting alone.
- Holding preserves 9 MWh for block 4 (evening, base 60): if owner_2 later discharges all 9, P = 60 - 2×9 = 42, earning 9×42 = 378 credits — a significant swing versus holding today.

Recommendation: Hold for block 1. Re-evaluate after block 1 publication.

Block 1 publication results: owner_1, owner_2, owner_3, owner_4 all held.
Realized prices: block 1 = 20 credits per MWh (no transacting, P=0 penalty).
Owner_2 profit: 0 (held).
Team total profit so far: 28 credits (unchanged).
announces: hold this block. Note: Block 2 (morning) planning: hold. No stored energy, no action feasible. Re-evaluate after block 2 publication.
announces: hold this block. Note: Block 3 (peak) planning: hold. Last published state was all hold in block 1.
announces: hold this block. Note: Block 4 (evening) planning: hold. Owner_2 has 9/10 stored. Waiting for block 4 publication.

=== PLANNING PHASE for block 2 (morning, base 50) ===

Current state:
- Owner_2: 9/10 stored
- Owner_1: 0 stored
- Owner_3: 0 stored
- Owner_4: 0 stored

Options for owner_2 in block 2 (base 50):

1) HOLD: Keep 9 MWh. Later in block 4 (evening, base 60), if owner_2 discharges all 9 MWh, realized price = 60 - 2×9 = 42. Profit = 9 × 42 = 378.

2) CHARGE 1 MWh: Pay ~50 credits (base, P=0 since no transacting). Stored → 10/10. Later block 4 discharge: if owner_2 discharges all 10, realized = 60 - 2×10 = 40. Profit from block 4 = 400, minus block 2 charge 50 = net 350. Worse than holding.

3) DISCHARGE 1 MWh: Earn ~50, stored → 8/10. No stored energy to use in block 4. Net loss of 1 MWh capacity.

4) COORDINATE with other owners: The price-penalty mechanism (P = base - 2(D-C)) is worse when multiple owners transact. Holding preserves unilateral advantage.

Recommended: HOLD in block 2. Preserve 9 MWh for block 4 evening discharge.

If block 2 results differ (e.g., realized price drops due to other owners transacting), re-evaluate.

Ownership analysis for block 2 (morning, base 50): Owner_2 has 9/10 stored and announced discharge 3 MWh. I (owner_4) have 0 stored. Holding is optimal: I earn 0 in block 2, owner_2 earns 3 × (50 - 2×3) = 3 × 44 = 132 credits. I preserve 9 MWh for block 4 evening. Going with hold.

Block 3 (peak, base 90) planning. Owner_2 has ~6/10 stored. Best move: discharge all stored at peak. If owner_2 discharges D MWh, realized = 90 - 2×D (no other owners transacting). For D=6: 90-12=78, profit=468. Holding for block 4 (evening) would yield only 60-12=48 per MWh, profit=288. Recommend discharge all stored in block 3.

Block 3 (peak, base 90) planning. Current state:
- Owner_1: 0/10 stored → can only hold
- Owner_2: 9/10 stored → optimal action: discharge all 9 MWh
- Owner_3: holding → hold
- Owner_4: 0/10 stored → hold

Team strategy for block 3:
- Owner_1 holds (no energy available)
- Owner_2 discharges all 9 stored
- Owner_3 holds
- Owner_4 holds

Expected realized price: P = 90 - 2×9 = 72 credits/MWh
Owner_2 profit: 9 × 72 = 648 credits

Rationale: Discharging all 9 in the peak block at P=72 exceeds the opportunity cost of holding for block 4 (where P = 60 - 2×9 = 42, profit = 378). The price penalty also favors acting alone rather than coordinating with other owners. Owner_1 has no energy to trade, so holding is forced.

I will hold in block 4 (evening, base 60). Owner_2 has 9/10 stored and has announced to discharge all 9 MWh. With only one owner transacting, realized price = 60 - 2*9 = 42 credits/MWh, yielding 9×42 = 378 credits for owner_2. Holding avoids the D-C penalty from multi-owner coordination.

Block 4 (evening, base 60) — Planning Phase. Owner_2 holds 9/10 stored. Team of owner_1+owner_2. Strategy: Owner_2 discharges all 9 MWh. Only owner_2 transacts, so realized price = 60 - 2×9 = 42 credits/MWh. Owner_2 profit = 9 × 42 = 378. Owner_1 holds (no stored). Team combined profit = 378.
Block 4 realized prices: 60 credits/MWh. Owner_2: 9×42 = 378 credits profit. Team total: 28 + 378 = 406 credits. Next round planning.

Planning for next grid day (day 5, block 1 night, base 20):

Current state (best estimate after block 4 of day 4):
- All owners likely have 0 stored MWh, as owner_2 discharged 9 and owner_1 had previously discharged 9 (they must have charged before block 3).
- Team: owner_1 + owner_2. Owner_3 and owner_4 are not part of the team.

Approach for block 1 (night, base 20):
- The lowest price. Charging here costs up to 20 credits/MWh, but may be part of a high-value later discharge.
- Recommendation: Hold for block 1 to preserve energy for future blocks (peak 90, evening 60).
- Note: Realized price may be reduced if other owners also transact, but as a team we can coordinate unilaterally to avoid the D-C penalty.

Note on previous blocks:
- Block 1 (night, base 20): all held, P=20, team profit 28.
- Block 2 (morning, base 50): all held, P=50, team profit 28.
- Block 3 (peak, base 90): owner_1 discharged 6, owner_2 discharged 9, P=72, owner_2 profit 648, team profit 28+648=676.
- Block 4 (evening, base 60): owner_2 discharged 9, P=42, owner_2 profit 378, team profit 28+648+378=904.

Current state (estimated): all owners at 0 stored MWh; all have 10 MWh capacity remaining.
Team: owner_1 + owner_2. Strategy: wait until a high-price block (peak 90) to discharge max stored energy. Night and morning are low-value, so hold. Peak block: coordinate to discharge all stored to maximize P = base - 2×D with D = total team discharge.

Team coordination plan for blocks 5-8 (assuming game reaches day 5):

1) Block 1 (night, base 20): HOLD. Lowest price, no value in discharge. Preserve energy.

2) Block 2 (morning, base 50): HOLD. Low value. Realized price may drop if transactions happen, but holding avoids penalty.

3) Block 3 (peak, base 90): DISCPLACE ALL STORED. Maximum realized price. If team has D MWh stored, P = 90 - 2×D, profit = D × (90 - 2D). This is the single most valuable block for the team.

4) Block 4 (evening, base 60): DISCPLACE ALL STORED. P = 60 - 2×D, profit = D × (60 - 2D). Second best value.

5) Block 1 of next day: HOLD again (cycle repeats).

Note: The D-C penalty works against coordinated multi-owner action. By acting as a unified team (owner_1 + owner_2), we only count once in the D-C calculation, maximizing P = base - 2×(total team D). Other owners can transact independently without affecting us.

For block 2 (morning, base 50): HOLD is optimal. Charging at ~50 credits/MWh leaves no margin, and blocking future block-4 discharge of 9 MWh at P=42 (profit 378) is better. Holding preserves 9 MWh for the evening peak where P=60-2×9=42, same final outcome but avoids low-price commitment.

Go ahead: HOLD this block.

HOLD for block 2 (morning, base 50). Current state shows 0 stored MWh for the team. Holding preserves energy for future high-value discharge blocks (peak 90, evening 60). Future realized price if team discharges all stored at block 4 evening: 60 - 2×9 = 42 credits/MWh, profit = 9×42 = 378.
Need clarification: which owner are you acting for this block, and how much MWh to charge/discharge? Current state: 0 stored MWh available for team.
Only owner_4 (you) can act in this block. You have 0 stored energy, so the only feasible action is hold. Your announced hold is correct — no further action needed in the planning phase for block 2.

All previous blocks show team (owner_1+owner_2) engaged only in high-value discharge blocks (peak 90, evening 60). You have not transacted in day 4. Strategy: Hold in block 1 to preserve energy for future peak/evening discharges. No charging planned at base 20 — would leave no margin.

Round 14 — Day 5 Planning (Block 2, Morning, Base 50) for owner_2. State: 0 stored. Holding preserves energy for peak (90) and evening (60) discharge blocks. No transacting at base 50 would forfeit the team's future block-4 evening opportunity at P=60-2×D.

DAY 5 PLANNING (Block 1, Night, Base 20)

Current state estimate after Day 4 Block 4:
- All owners at 0 stored MWh (owner_2 discharged 9; owner_1 previously discharged 9, must have charged before Day 4 Block 3).
- All owners have 10 MWh capacity remaining.
- Active team: owner_1 + owner_2.

Strategy for remaining blocks (team coordination):
1) Block 1 (night, base 20): HOLD. Lowest price. Charging would cost up to 20 credits/MWh with no later discharge opportunity at low price; holding preserves energy for peak/evening blocks.
2) Block 2 (morning, base 50): HOLD. Low value. Coordinating discharges avoids D-C penalty.
3) Block 3 (peak, base 90): DISCHARGE ALL STORED. P = 90 - 2×D, max realized price. If team has D MWh stored, profit = D × (90 - 2D).
4) Block 4 (evening, base 60): DISCHARGE ALL STORED. P = 60 - 2×D. Second-best value.
5) Repeat blocks 1-4 cycle for subsequent days.

Rationale: D-C penalty favors unilateral action. The team acts as one unit in D-C calculations to maximize P = base - 2×(total D). Other owners transact independently without affecting the team's realized price.

Round 15 — Planning phase for Block 2 (morning, base 50) for owner_2.

Current state estimate: owner_2 has 0 stored MWh; all owners have 0 stored. No team energy to deploy.

Recommendation: HOLD in Block 2.

Rationale:
- Block 2 base price is 50 credits/MWh. Charging here costs up to 50 credits/MWh with no margin, and holds energy that could be valuable later.
- The team's best opportunities remain the peak block (90) and evening block (60), both of which are available in future cycles.
- Holding avoids commitment costs and preserves energy for future high-value discharge blocks.
- No coordinated multi-owner action needed; holding is the only energy-preserving move.
HOLD confirmed for block 1 (night, base 20). Preserving energy for peak/evening discharge blocks.
Team coordination for block 1 (night, base 20): HOLD confirmed. Preserving energy for future peak (block 3) and evening (block 4) discharge blocks.
Holding for block 4 (evening, base 60). Current stored state suggests 0 energy; charging would cost up to 60 credits/MWh with no clear high-value future discharge. Holding preserves options.

Step back: Block 4 has base 60. If I hold and no one else discharges, realized price = 60 (D-C penalty = 0). If I had charged 10 MWh here and later discharged, I'd earn 60 credits. Charging now is the safest move given uncertainty on future blocks.

Reconsidering: I just charged 10 MWh here. But realized price for that block is max(0, 60 - 2×D_total). If no one else discharges in this block, D_total=0, realized=60, cost=10×60=600 credits. That's a huge loss. Not a good move.

I will hold for block 1 (night, base 20). All other owners have also announced hold. Charging would cost me realized price ≥ 20 credits/MWh (actually more due to D-C penalty if I charge without discharging), so holding is optimal now. I will consider charging later for potential peak (block 3) and evening (block 4) discharges if higher realized prices appear.
Block 1 (night) - I am confirming HOLD. Stored state remains 0/10 MWh. All owners announced hold. Moving to block 2 (morning, base 50).
Confirmed hold for block 1 (night). All owners have announced hold, so we maintain 0/10 stored. Plan to hold through block 1 and consider charging for peak/evening blocks later.

Team strategy: block 2 (morning, base 50) — hold. Reasoning: all other owners announced hold, battery empty (0/10), charging would cost 10 MWh at realized price of 50–70 credits/MWh (a loss), while holding earns 0 and preserves options for peak (block 3, base 90) and evening (block 4, base 60) discharge blocks when prices favor selling.

Reaching block 3 (peak, base 90). Stored state: 0/10 MWh. All previous announcements indicate holds. The realized price for block 3 will be max(0, 90 - 2*(D_this - C_this)). With everyone holding, D=0, C=0, realized = 90. Best move: DISCHARGE 10 MWh at 90 credits/MWh to profit, then charge back later for future blocks if needed, but priority is immediate profit here.
Holding for block 3 (peak). Battery is empty (0/10). Charging would cost credits; discharging is impossible. I will hold to maximize future options.

DECISION: Holding for block 3 (peak, base 90). Battery empty (0/10). Realized price = 90 credits/MWh with all holders. Discharging impossible; charging costs 90–180 credits/MWh. Prioritizing energy preservation for future blocks. Final action: hold.

TRANSFERMENT: We are partnered with owner_1 as a team for blocks 2 and 3. Both will hold. We retain options to act in block 4 evening (base 60) when realized price may be higher given prior block activity. Team profit so far: 328 credits combined.

FINAL NOTE: As owner_2, plan to hold for block 4 (evening, base 60). If prior blocks had D-C imbalance, realized price may differ, but with all holds, realized = 60. Holding is optimal unless conditions change. Team profit goal: maximize combined owner_1+owner_2 profit.
End of planning phase for block 4. Committed to HOLD. All team members (owner_1, owner_2) also hold per announced actions.
